summary: Design panel for issue 513 unit 2: three independent designs, three lens judges, one synthesis

designs.name: Design A: ODS-allowlist mint, literal exact-triple binding, reviewed stray pins, refold-invariant re-bind
designs.summary:
This is the strongest version I can make of the literal-binding approach. It takes in every finding from the wf_4e7d846d review. Its value on its own is weak, and the design says so.

(1) A frozen ODS allowlist, built from a 2026-10-11 snapshot. It holds every Active RC1 three-character code in the digit-rule family (letters only, or digits that are all 0) for these roles: NHS trust RO197 (163), ICB RO261 with a Q lead (39), CSU RO213 (8). It adds the care trusts TAD and TAJ and the measured IS provider DQF, for 213 entries. It contains no RO98 (sub-ICB/CCG) code and no Inactive code. An O/0 fold maps a tail onto the allowlisted spelling only when exactly one variant is in the list. Across all 931 three-character ODS codes I found zero O/0 twins, so the fold cannot collide. The arm returns (GB, national, GBNHS<code>) whatever the mention's country. The allowlist is the whole gate: idgate::condemns can never fire on this shape.

(2) Binding is literal and exact-triple, like every digit-bearing NHS code today. There is no name gate.

(3) Strays get a remedy that survives a rebuild: a reviewed per-(triple, name_norm) verdict table, org_identifier_name_verdicts. The resolver reads it at open. A mention whose exact triple and org_name_norm are pinned 'stray' takes the issue-234 name path, exactly as it binds today. This keeps all 72 adjudicated stray mentions where they are and refuses 0 SAME mentions. It does not protect strays nobody has reviewed yet. A standing census delta catches those, and the unreviewed-bind counter feeds it.

(4) A census gate runs before prevention ships. It is a dry, in-app census of every GBNHS+3 raw value. It calls the same allowlist function the normaliser will call. Every holder is listed (no 5-holder cap), and every (identity, name_norm) pair with a coded mention is adjudicated. The gate rules G1–G5 must pass before the normaliser arm deploys.

(5) The re-bind is refold-invariant. It is a dry-first job whose end state equals a from-archive rebuild under the new normaliser. It moves only mentions on identifier-NULL orgs and excludes rehomed mentions and orgs under review.
- A cluster emptied whole is retired merge-shaped: repoint_org_references, DELETE, an org_merge_log row under the new rule 'nhs-ods', and change events. Its old id answers 308.
- A partially emptied cluster keeps its uncoded mentions as the body's provisional twin. The moved mentions' Tenders are stamped stale.
- Identity orgs take their ODS name through a resolver hook. The head name is therefore the same in a rebuild as in ingest, and does not depend on mint order or race.

(6) Prevention and the re-bind ship together. They deploy only when 469 U7 can follow in the same window.

The honest bottom line, from the sample of 380 adjudicated holder orgs:
- Coded mentions are a median 9.5% of a body's mentions.
- Orgs go 355 → 447 after the re-bind → 332 after U7, a net 6.5%. Twelve codes end up worse.
- After U7 the canonical row holds a median 29.3% of its body. It is the body's largest org for only 40 of 128 bodies.
- The body's largest single org shrinks for 109 of 128 bodies.
- No uncoded spelling split is repaired.

A's real value is twofold. It gives an ODS identity key that ?identifier= answers and that 469 U7 can pair with the PPON. And it stops future coded mentions splitting by spelling. It is cheap to reverse: a code revert plus the symmetric re-bind, or a rebuild. It is a substrate that design C (verdict-driven twin consolidation) could later build on, not a fix in itself.

units.title: U1 — Frozen ODS allowlist module (pure, no behaviour change)
units.what:
New ingest module holding a sorted static table of three-character ODS organisation codes in the digit-rule family (letters only, or zero-only), each with its ODS name and role id. A provenance header records the ORD list endpoints, the role ids, the snapshot date (2026-10-11) and the counts.

Membership:
- Status=Active and RC1 at the snapshot, roles RO197, RO261 with a Q lead, RO213 and RO107. That gives 210 codes plus TAD and TAJ.
- RO172 IS providers only when measured by the census: DQF now; AAV only if the census and adjudication confirm it.
- Never RO98: sub-ICB and CCG codes, including the 18 zero-only `00[A-Z]` codes, belong to 519.
- Never Inactive codes. RCN and RMB, the only two seen, sit on the wrong trusts.
- A census-measured exception list for an Inactive code whose ODS legal end falls after the notices that published it (none found yet).
- Legally-ended but Active predecessors (QJG QMJ QMM QNQ QXU RNK RYV) stay: they are real bodies whose pre-2026-04 notices are theirs.

API:
- `nhs_ods_org_code(value) -> Option<Hit{identity, folded}>` for a normalised 8-character `GBNHS???` value. It takes the exact tail, or the single O/0 variant that is listed. The fold sits behind a const switch so G4 can ship it disabled.
- `nhs_ods_name(identity) -> Option<&'static str>`.

The generator script stays in `.scratch/tender-db/513-nhs/`; the table is code, like countries.rs and 469 U3's REGISTRIES shapes.

units.title: U2 — Stray-pin verdict table and resolver read (store; inert with no rows)
units.what:
A per-(identity triple, name_norm) verdict: 'stray' means the mention is not this code's body, 'same' means it was reviewed as the body.
- Schema: `org_identifier_name_verdicts(identifier, identifier_kind, country, name_norm, cohort, verdict CHECK IN ('same','stray'), rationale, confidence, reviewed_at, PRIMARY KEY(identifier, identifier_kind, country, name_norm))`.
- It is keyed by triple, never by org id, so it survives a from-archive rebuild, as org_identifier_verdicts does.
- POST /admin/identifier-name-verdicts computes name_norm server-side with `org_name_norm`. Its validator accepts only allowlisted GB national GBNHS identities for this issue, so a pin is inert until prevention ships.
- Resolver open loads 'stray' rows into a HashSet. `resolve_one_mention` treats a mention whose (triple, org_name_norm(name)) is pinned as identifier-less. It skips org_of, rekey, canon and alias, and takes the issue-234 (name_norm, country, identifier IS NULL) path, where it lands on exactly the cluster it sits in today.
- New diag line `[issue 513] pinned binds N; allowlisted binds with no name verdict M`. M feeds the standing census delta.
- This is the first mechanism that unbinds an exact triple for named mentions. 452's documented rule "the exact triple still binds" becomes "unless a stray pin names this mention's name"; update the comment.

units.title: U4 — Adjudication campaign and verdict posting (data, no code; the census gate)
units.what:
Adjudicate every (identity, name_norm) pair the census lists with at least one coded mention, using the wf_a168eb50 protocol: one claimant plus one independent skeptic. This includes the 35 holders the cap hid and the not-yet-listed tails (RWK, and the fold hits ROB and Q0X).
- Post 'same' for SAME and HOSTED_OR_SITE, and 'stray' for DIFFERENT and NOT_ORG. An unresolved disagreement posts 'stray', which is the status quo.
- Post 469 keep verdicts (GB:altid key `GB-NHS:<identity>~<ppon>`) for the cross-body PPON pairs: QKK~PCXT8262NYRV, QMF~PMLZ8385VMTM, RXX~PBCW8913JCZL, RTF~PLMV4859MQXP, RGT~(Teleflex), 0CX~(TEST), RAL~(trading-as).
- Then apply gate rules G1–G5 (see stop_rules). Prevention does not ship until they pass.

units.title: U5 — Prevention and the re-bind job (ONE deploy; only after U4's gate and with 469 U7 built)
units.what:
(a) Normaliser arm. In `normalise_identifier_with`, AFTER the ASCII filter and BEFORE the digit rule: when `folds` holds, the value is 8 characters and starts with `GBNHS`, and `nhs_ods_org_code` hits, return `Identifier{country: Some("GB"), kind: "national", value: hit.identity}`.
- The country is forced to GB, fixing the review's country-less twin finding.
- `normalise_identifier_before_folds` stays unchanged.

(b) Designated-name hook. `Db::arm_designated_names(&mut resolver, fn(&str) -> Option<&'static str>)`, armed on the fold resolvers the way arm_altid_alias is. When a mint is for a triple the hook names, the resolver takes the ODS name as head name and name_norm; the mention's name still feeds organization_names. Rebuild and ingest therefore name the identity org identically, whatever minted first.

(c) Job `rebind-nhs-ods` (dry, then wet), symmetric:
- Forward: each mention on an identifier-NULL org whose raw_identifier now normalises to an allowlisted identity and is not pinned moves to that identity's org.
- Reverse: each mention on an identity org that a stray pin now covers moves to the name-path org: the lowest-id identifier-NULL row with that (name_norm, GB), or a new provisional, as the 234 path does.
- Excluded: org_mention_rehoming rows and orgs in org_ids_under_review. Coded mentions on identifier-bearing orgs are counted (`held_by_identified`), not moved.
- The dry plan stores the tuples (notice, section, from, to), grouped per source org as full, partial or split.

Wet:
- It holds against the stored tuples, the apply_rehoming pattern. A mention already at its destination counts as `already_placed`.
- Missing identity orgs are minted through the same mint and designated name.
- FULL clusters (every mention goes to one identity, every pair 'same'): collect touched Tenders, `repoint_org_references(identity, cluster, 'nhs-ods')`, DELETE the cluster, write `org_merge_log(keep, loser, 'nhs-ods', evidence{identity, name_norm, moved, cohort}, job, at)`, then `organization removed`/`changed` and `tender changed` changes, all in the window transaction (the rekey arm's shape; ADR-0017 D5).
- A cluster the orphan sweep already took (it is in org_sweep_log): write only the ledger row, so its id still answers 308 through resolve_org.
- PARTIAL clusters: UPDATE the mention row (guarded on `organization_id = from`) and `stamp_tenders_of_notices_stale` in the same transaction. The next `project` rebuilds the party rows ("only the mention moves, everything else is re-derived").
- Split clusters are held.

  - GBNHSICB, 00P, TBC, RCN and RBLN give None.

designs.measured_effect:
All numbers below were computed from the data files in /home/user/tender-db/.scratch/tender-db/513-nhs/u1. The scripts are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-tender-db/3050fd14-5ca6-5dd7-8b63-f827e13fd8ce/scratchpad/panel/A/ (a1_allowlist.py … a5_split.py, run with python3 -I). The scope is the 380 adjudicated holder orgs and their 61,497 mentions, not the corpus. Corpus-wide figures are U3's job.

**Allowlist**
- 931 distinct three-character codes across the RO197/RO261/RO213/RO98 lists. 0 O/0 twin pairs.
- Digit-rule-family, Active, RC1: RO197 163, RO261 (all Q-led) 39, RO213 8 = 210. Plus TAD, TAJ, DQF = 213.
- Excluded: 246 Inactive family codes (RO197 215, RO261 3, RO213 28), and all 18 zero-only RO98 codes (10 of them Active, including 00N and 00P).

**Tails on the holder orgs**
- 150 distinct GBNHS+3 tails, all digit-rule family.
- The arm mints 131 tails: 128 of the listed codes, RWK, and the fold hits ROB→R0B and Q0X→QOX. That is 129 identities from 7,498 coded mentions.
- It refuses 19 tails (44 mentions):
  - all 16 junk tails the withdrawn shape rule would mint: ICB, 00N, 00P, OYG, ODX, 0YD, OYD, QYC, QKJ, QLG, RGY, UHS, KGH, NGH, RCN, RMB;
  - NHS and TBC;
  - AAV, a real IS code (5 mentions); the census decides whether it is added.
- The withdrawn shape rule would have minted 148 tails, 17 of them junk.
- Out of reach: 75 bare 3-letter values (RTD 29, RGT 12, RHW 12, …), refused by length at project.rs:8710; plus 44 longer GBNHS strings (typed names).

**Strays**
- Pins cover 22 (code, holder) pairs in 20 codes, 72 coded mentions (0.96% of 7,498). All of them stay where they are.
- Without pins, 5 non-SAME clusters would be emptied and redirected into another body: Alder Hey 30968741 into RET/Walton, Leeds Teaching Hospital Trust 31565965 into RAE/Bradford, Sustainable Energy First 31610393 into RWF, the QJG crisis service 31602019, and the RHM coroners title 30926652.
- Per-code stray share before pins: REN 68%, RET 64%, RXX 50%, RAE 43%.
- Comparison with B (gate_sim.py re-run, same numbers as the review): B refuses 66 of 72 strays automatically, but also 109 SAME (106 of them RWW's rename) and 3 HOSTED. A refuses 0 SAME and keeps all 72 known strays out, but cannot see strays that appear later.

**Moves**
- 7,426 coded mentions move (7,411 SAME + 15 HOSTED) from 245 clusters.
- 219 of them move by merge-shaped retirement of 42 fully emptied clusters (36 SAME, 6 HOSTED: RHQ, REM, RJL ×2, RAL, RHA). No cluster splits across two identities.
- 7,207 move from 203 partially moved clusters, which stay as twins.
- 11 codes were capped at 5 listed holders (QHM 16, QYG 11, QMF 10, QKK 8, QRL 8, QOQ 7, QMJ/RBL/RBN/RJZ/RWW 6), so 35 holders are unmeasured.

**Org counts** (SAME registry clusters plus SAME PPON orgs, 131 codes including DQF)
- 355 today → 447 after the re-bind → 332 after U7. The review said 448 before U7; my recomputation gives 447. Pins do not change these counts.
- Per registry-side code (130), after U7: 93 unchanged, 25 better, 12 worse. The worse ones are 0CX, QJG, QKK, QMF, QOX, QYG, RAL, RGT, RJN, RTF, RXM and RXX.

**Coverage, the weak part**
- On SAME clusters (distinct orgs): 7,408 coded mentions, against 47,467 uncoded and 415 other-identifier mentions.
- Median coded share of a body's SAME registry mentions: 9.5%. 66 of 128 bodies are below 10%. The review's 9.7% is over 130 codes.
- After U7, the canonical org (identity org plus its single SAME PPON org) holds a median 29.3% of its body. It is the largest org for only 40 of 128 bodies.
- The body's largest single org shrinks for 109 of 128 bodies; the median largest-org share goes from 82.0% to 71.6%.
- Readers of the main spelling cluster lose the coded (mostly recent FTS) notices to the identity org, and nothing links the two.
designs.refold_invariance:
A from-archive rebuild under this design produces the same mention partition as the wet re-bind, by construction.

**What a rebuild keeps and drops**
- It DROPs and recreates organizations, organization_mentions and organization_names, and deletes organization_merged_identifiers and org_name_drops (canonical.rs:12045-12075).
- It keeps notices, every verdict table and org_merge_log. Verdicts are keyed by triple precisely because org ids are re-minted (canonical.rs:645-651), and the alias "survives the renumbering of a bare rebuild while org_merge_log persists" (canonical.rs:6874-6878, 15880-15890).
- It resolves mentions in notice-id order (project.rs:2042-2045).

**Under the new code**
- (1) Every unpinned coded mention normalises to (GB, national, GBNHS<code>) and binds by exact triple through org_of (canonical.rs:16770). The first such mention mints the identity org (17271-17283), with the designated ODS name from the hook. The head therefore does not depend on which mention came first, or on ingest racing the job.
- (2) Pinned and uncoded mentions take the issue-234 path. It reuses the lowest-id `name_norm = ? AND country = ? AND identifier IS NULL` row (canonical.rs:17358), which forms exactly the provisional twins that the wet job leaves standing.
- (3) Clusters whose every mention is coded never form in a rebuild. The wet job retires them merge-shaped, so the live table matches. Their org_merge_log 'nhs-ods' rows only redirect old ids. After a rebuild they dangle like every pre-rebuild ledger row, and the era floor already handles that (canonical.rs:4981-4986).
- (4) Pins persist as verdict rows read at resolver open (beside the 453 `rekeyed` preload, canonical.rs:15713-15727). So a rebuild binds a pinned stray by name, as the live table does.
- (5) U7's merges replay without a merge job. The e2-altid ledger row carries registry_scheme/kind/identity, so after a rebuild the register alias binds PPON-first mentions straight to the identity org and records the PPON as a merged identifier (canonical.rs:17247-17262, issue 460 D5).
- (6) A refold alone never re-decides a recorded mention (publishes() compares only name, country, raw_identifier and scheme; canonical.rs:10255-10269). That is why the explicit job exists. A later 434 refresh of a moved mention re-resolves to the same place, because prevention, pins and the job share one rule.
- (7) The job is symmetric: a new pin, an allowlist addition or a removal re-runs it in either direction. A code revert plus the reverse run, or a rebuild, restores today's state. Nothing in A needs an unmerge tool.

**Remaining gaps, which the dry plan names**
- Coded mentions held by identifier-bearing orgs: 0 in the sample. They are counted, not moved; U7 converges them.
- Mentions placed by rehoming or case verdicts are excluded from the move. A rebuild already loses those placements today, because the resolver does not read org_mention_rehoming.
- Head names of twin clusters follow first-mention order, as they always have.
designs.false_merge_risk:
**Org-level merges.** The only org deletions are the merge-shaped retirements, and they need all three of:
- every mention of the cluster moves to ONE identity;
- every (identity, name_norm) pair in it was adjudicated 'same' (SAME or HOSTED_OR_SITE) at the census;
- the wet tuples equal the dry plan.

In the sample that is 42 clusters: 36 SAME, and 6 hosted units or sites folded into their legal host trust. That is correct under CONTEXT.md, where an Organization is one profile per real-world entity, but a site's own label survives only as a satellite name. The 5 wrong-body retirements the withdrawn design would have made (Alder Hey into Walton, among others) cannot happen: pins keep their mentions, so those clusters never empty.

**Mention-level mis-binding** is the residual risk.
- Literal name-blind binding sends every unreviewed stray to the wrong body's identity org until the next census delta pins it. The sample rate is 0.96% of coded mentions, but the stray-prone capped codes showed 12.7% DIFFERENT holders against 5.6% elsewhere. Each case misattributes a mention or Tender on served data; it never fuses two org rows.
- It is bounded by the unreviewed-bind counter (U2), the monthly delta (S7) and the reverse re-bind.
- The ICB-on-two-ICBs fusion cannot happen: ICB is not allowlisted.

**The O/0 fold** is name-blind but confined to a closed list with zero twins. The measured fold hits (4 mentions) are both SAME, and G4 ships the fold disabled if any census fold hit is not SAME.

**U7 cross-body pairs.** QKK and QMF (the swapped London ICBs), RXX (Sussex PPON), RTF (NHFM PPON), RGT (Teleflex), 0CX (TEST) and RAL (trading-as) are hard-denied by keep verdicts posted before U7. The U5 wet branch merges only under HIGH admitting verdicts, and the pins keep stray names out of the identity orgs that U7's corroboration reads.

**Mentions not moved.** Pinning is status quo, so an unresolved adjudication defaults to 'stray' and the error direction is a missed move, never a false move.
designs.stop_rules:
**CENSUS GATE: all must pass before the U5 normaliser arm deploys.**
- **G1 coverage:** 100% of (allowlisted identity, name_norm) pairs with ≥1 coded mention in the corpus carry a posted name verdict from claimant plus skeptic, including the 35 holders the cap hid. Any gap means no deploy.
- **G2 precision:** every allowlisted code that occurs in the corpus has ≥1 'same' pair. A code whose pairs are all 'stray' is removed from the allowlist before deploy.
- **G3 one ruler:** the census decision equals `nhs_ods_org_code` on every distinct tail; no tail outside the allowlist would mint. Any listed tail that ODS answers as an Active RC1 trust/ICB/CSU of its holder's body is either added (re-census) or recorded as refused.
- **G4 fold:** every fold-hit pair is 'same'. Otherwise the fold ships disabled.
- **G5 go/no-go:**
  - 469 U7's prerequisites (REGISTRIES NHS shape, pin-aware first_bound) are on main and its verdict campaign is staffed for the same window. The 355 → 447 interim must last one window, not weeks.
  - The census reports the median coded share for notices from the last 12 months. If it is not above the all-time 9.5%, A's forward value is not growing, and the decision returns to the panel (design C).

**WET RE-BIND** (dry plan read first)
- **S1 parity:** the live tuples (notice, section, from, to) equal the dry plan's stored tuples (the apply_rehoming / 453 pattern). Mentions already at their destination count as `already_placed`. Any other difference refuses the whole run.
- **S2 no unreviewed move:** every moved (identity, name_norm) has a 'same' verdict. A new name since the census holds that identity's moves.
- **S3 retirement:** only clusters with one target identity and only 'same' pairs (42 expected, 0 split). Anything else holds without deleting.
- **S4 scope:** moves come only from identifier-NULL orgs; `held_by_identified`, the rehomed and under-review exclusions, and Tenders touched are reported. Stop if `held_by_identified` exceeds 1% of moves (0 in the sample).
- **S5 ledger and API read:**
  - every retired id answers MergedInto(identity) (read.rs:4841);
  - every identity org has the ODS head name and country GB;
  - `?identifier=GBNHS<code>` answers for a sample of 20;
  - pinned strays (Alder Hey 30968741, Leeds Teaching Hospital Trust 31565965, Walton under REN on 1371484) are unmoved.

The pin table gives 519 option (c) a mention-level mechanism for neighbour-code strays on digit codes; transpositions such as RF1→R1F remain 453 re-key material. 519 should land before or with U7, so that each NHS body pairs one register org.

designs.open_risks:
1. **The net effect is weak and partly regressive.**
   - Coded mentions are a median 9.5% of a body's mentions.
   - After U7 the canonical row holds a median 29.3%, and is the largest org for only 40 of 128 bodies.
   - 109 of 128 bodies' largest org shrinks: the main spelling cluster loses its coded, mostly recent FTS notices. This breaks cross-era continuity, with nothing linking twin and canonical.
   - Twelve codes are worse even after U7, and nothing in A repairs an uncoded spelling split.
   - Mitigations are outside A: an E3 'see also' edge on the API, or design C's verdict-driven consolidation on top of A's identity.
2. **Strays nobody has reviewed yet bind wrongly between census deltas.** A's protection is review cadence, not a gate. If S7's unreviewed-bind rate runs above about 1%, B's best-match ODS gate becomes the better trade.
3. **The sample is not the corpus.** All numbers come from the 380 holder orgs of PPON-paired codes, with 35 holders hidden by the cap. Corpus-wide tails, holders, country-less mentions and time profile are unknown until U3 runs, and G1's adjudication load could be much larger than the 393 claims of unit 1.
4. **The allowlist will go stale.** New letter-only trusts or ICBs after 2026-10-11 stay name-bound until a census refresh. The 2026-04 ICB successors carry digit codes and already mint. Inactive FTS-era codes are excluded unless the census measures them.
5. **Pins depend on name_norm.** Pins are keyed by org_name_norm (issue 432). Changing that function would orphan pins and need a re-key pass. A pin also covers only one spelling: Alder Hey under a new spelling binds Walton until the next delta.
6. **Ingest can race the job.** Between deploy and the wet run, a 434 refresh or new ingest can move mentions piecemeal. An emptied cluster swept first loses its 404-free redirect unless the ledger-only row is written. S1's `already_placed` and the org_sweep_log check cover both, but they need tests.
7. **Retiring hosted units and sites folds named buying points** (a hospital site, a commercial hub) into the host trust's identity. The site name survives only as a satellite, and only when the language slot is free.
8. **Bare 3-letter values** (75 mentions on these orgs) and typed names never mint. The scheme is deliberately not passed to the normaliser (project.rs:4962-4973).
9. **The ODS uppercase head name** becomes what the API serves. It is accurate but differs from publishers' usage.
10. **Removing an allowlisted code later** sends its identity org's mentions back to several clusters. There is no single redirect target, so the old identity id would 404 after the orphan sweep.

designs.summary:
Mint (GB, national, GBNHS<code>) only for codes on a frozen ODS allowlist, and only for mentions whose name passes a best-match check against a frozen ODS name table. Everything else binds by name, exactly as today.

**Allowlist.** Active RC1 three-character ODS organisation codes with primary role RO197 (trust), RO107 (care trust), RO261 (ICB), RO213 (CSU), or RO172 where measured (DQF). Only tails that the digit rule or the all-zero rule refuses today (project.rs:8710, :8715) are covered. That is 213 codes in the 2026-10-11 table. A tail outside the list may take one O↔0 swap, and only when exactly one allowlisted variant exists. No O/0 twin pair exists among the 1,053 ODS codes in the table.

**The check (pure, deterministic).** It reads the mention's head name (the same fact `publishes()` stores), the raw value and the country. It refuses when:
- the name carries an agent marker (c/o, on behalf of);
- the name declares a role the code contradicts (ICB, CSU or trust words against the code's ODS primary role);
- the name shares no distinctive token with any of the code's names. Matching is prefix-tolerant from 6 characters (cambridge ~ cambridgeshire);
- the code's best name covers less than half of the mention's distinctive tokens;
- another ODS code scores strictly higher on (role agreement, distinctive-token Jaccard, NHS-descriptor-token Jaccard), compared in that order. The rival set is every ODS code of those roles in the frozen table: 3- and 5-character, active and inactive, and sub-ICB, but not the code's own inactive predecessors.

A code's names are its current ODS name plus the names of its Inactive predecessors from ORD Succs. That is how RWW's "Warrington and Halton" spellings pass: they match RKC "Warrington Hospital NHS Trust" and RJS "Halton General Hospital NHS Trust".

**Where it lives.** The check is a pure function in ingest. It is injected into the resolver the way canon_key, norm and the altid alias are (project.rs:2033-2037). It runs in resolve_one_mention before `match &m.identifier` (canonical.rs:16767). An admitted mention takes the existing exact-triple path (16770 probe, 17271 mint). A refused one falls through to the issue-234 name arm (17314-17361), not to the mint that a 452/470 refusal takes (17295). The check runs before the triple lookup, so caching the triple in org_of after an admitted mint is safe. A guarded hit is never cached (17232), and this is the deliberate difference.

**Why not the projection.** It is not placed at the projection's identifier site (project.rs:4969), because m.identifier also feeds the plan's buyer_key and buyer-guard tokens (project.rs:7542-7563, :7620), so tender grouping would move on refold. The store reads Mention.identifier only at canonical.rs:16767.

**Order.**
1. A census ships first, with no prevention: it stores the check's verdict for every GB-NHS value and party name.
2. Then one deploy brings the arm, disarmed until its repair has run for the current table version, plus a repair job (dry, then wet) that moves the standing admitted mentions in notice order. The repair stamps tenders stale, and retires a fully emptied cluster with an org_merge_log redirect (rule 'nhs-ods').
3. 469 U7 then uses the same check as its witness corroboration for NHS pairs.

**Measured on the unit-1 sample.**
- Registry side: 7,400 of 7,402 SAME coded mentions admitted; 0 of 68 DIFFERENT and 0 of 4 NOT_ORG admitted; 9 of 15 HOSTED admitted (hosted units of the trust itself).
- PPON side: 116 of 116 SAME admitted, 0 of 5 DIFFERENT. QKK, QMF, RXX, RTF and RGT are all refused.
- 0 of 2,933 synthetic neighbour-code strays admitted.
- 0 junk mints.

Org counts barely differ from design A (355 → 449 → 334, against A's 447 → 332). What B buys is correctness: 0 strays and 0 non-SAME clusters move, against A's 72 and 5. It does not fix the "coded mentions are about 10% of a body" weakness. That twin problem stays with design C or a reviewed follow-up.

designs.refold_invariance:
**The verdict is a pure function.** nhs_ods_admit reads the raw value, the country and the head name — three of the four facts RecordedMention::publishes compares (canonical.rs:10264-10269) — plus a table compiled into the binary. It reads no database state.

This is unlike the 452/470 guarded path. That path reads the owners' current names from organizations and organization_names (canonical.rs:16893), so its answers depend on fold order.

**1. Refold of an unchanged recorded mention.** It keeps its org (canonical.rs:16762). Arming moves nothing on its own, by design; the 10256-10263 doc explains that re-deciding unchanged mentions would undo merges and rehomings. Only the repair moves standing mentions, and only those whose verdict says so.

**2. A re-parse that changes a mention's facts.** The issue-434 refresh re-resolves it through the same arm (stale path, 16758-16764), and the existing stamp (16408) rewrites its Tenders.

**3. A full rebuild from archives.** The recorded-mention preload is empty (16332), and mentions resolve in notice-id order (project.rs:2043-2046).
- Every admitted mention reaches the exact triple: the first mints (17271) with its own name, later ones bind through org_of.
- Every refused mention takes the issue-234 name arm: the lowest-id identifier-IS-NULL row with the same name_norm and country (17355-17361).

That is exactly the state the repair produces, given three things:
- the repair evaluates the same function on the same stored facts;
- it mints in ascending notice order with the earliest admitted name;
- the arm was not live before the repair. Arming only after a completed wet repair of the current table version ensures this, and a rebuild run after that arms too.

A cluster the repair retired never re-forms in a rebuild, because all its mentions are admitted. Its old id resolves through org_merge_log. resolve_org reads only that ledger (read.rs:4844-4869), and the ledger is kept across a rebuild (canonical.rs:6876-6879, 15884-15889).

**4. Merges and aliases.**
- U7's register merges write e2-altid ledger rows keyed by identity, not org id. The alias re-arms from the ledger and binds PPON mentions only through the exact (GB, national, GBNHS…) row (AltIdTarget::Registry, 6866-6874), so it survives renumbering.
- Altid verdicts are keyed `<scheme>:<identity>~<ppon>`.
- Identifier verdicts are triple-wide and read as triples at arming (7267-7287).
- Issue-362 merge verdicts are keyed by member org ids, so a renumbering rebuild leaves them stale. That is pre-existing and not introduced here.
- Rehomings are not re-applied by a rebuild: org_mention_rehoming is read only by the rehoming paths. So the repair skips rehomed mentions to respect the reviewer, and a rebuild would differ there exactly as it does for every org today.

**5. A table change** (an annual ODS refresh, a former-names entry) is a new version. It disarms the arm until that version's repair has run dry and wet. The fold and the standing state therefore never run under two rulers.

**What a refused mention does.** It is never cached and never mints an identifier-bearing row. It binds, or keeps, its name row exactly as today, so a stray such as Alder Hey under RET stays in the Alder Hey cluster. It is counted per reason in the fold log and listed in the census. A refusal is a missed merge, which is recoverable: a later table version or a reviewed verdict picks it up through the same repair.
designs.false_merge_risk:
**Mint risk.** Only allowlisted Active RC1 organisation codes can mint. In the sample:
- every non-allowlisted tail refuses: ICB on two ICBs, 00N/00P, TBC, NHS, and the typos OYG, ODX, QKJ, QLG, QYC;
- the O/0 fold routes ROB and Q0X onto the real code instead of minting a 470-style twin;
- no O/0 twin pair exists anywhere in the 1,053-code table;
- digit-bearing codes are untouched, and so is RO98: issue 519's splits do not grow.

**Bind risk.** Measured stray admissions are 0:
- registry side: 0 of 68 DIFFERENT and 0 of 4 NOT_ORG;
- PPON side: 0 of 5 DIFFERENT and 0 of 1 NOT_ORG;
- synthetic neighbour strays: 0 of 2,933 pairs.

The rival set includes inactive, five-character and sub-ICB names. A code that a successor took over refuses the successor's name: 'NHS West and North London ICB' under QMJ, 'North London NHS FT' under RNK.

The residual admitted class is HOSTED: 9 mentions, such as 'Royal Free … T/AS Transformation Partners', 'Leeds and York Partnership … trading as NOE CPC', and 'University Hospitals of Liverpool Group'. These are trading names or units of the code's own legal body, not a second body.

**Order-of-binding risk.** The check never reads owner names, so a stray cannot ride in on an earlier mention's name. The identity org's head is the earliest admitted name, and admitted names always pass the check.

**Cross-body via U7.** The same check applied to the witness party's name denies every flagged hazard: QKK↔QMF, RXX, RTF, RGT, 0CX.

**Where the risk remains:**
1. Overfitting. The tokeniser's role, descriptor, prefix-6, coverage-½ and agent rules were tuned on these 393 holders. The synthetic test reuses the same names, so the 35 unlisted holders and the corpus census are the blind test.
2. ODS code reuse or late renames that ODS records against the wrong code. The check compares against the current name, which limits but does not exclude this.
3. Ties. There are 0 in the sample, but a tie admits. Changing this to refuse is cheap if the census shows any.

A false merge here would be an admitted stray. The census stop rule C2 and the repair's dry-key hold gate it before any wet run, and the per-mention moves are reversible from the stored dry plan.
designs.stop_rules:
**Census, after U1 and before the arm ships:**
- C1, allowlist completeness. Any non-allowlisted three-character tail that is an Active RC1 organisation of an allowed role and carries 2 or more mentions → STOP: amend the table and re-run. The sample has one such tail, AAV (5 mentions, RO172); decide RO172 explicitly.
- C2, admission precision, blind. A reviewer plus a skeptic (the wf_a168eb50 rubric) adjudicate every admitted (code, name) pair outside the 393 holders already adjudicated, including the 35 never-listed holders in QHM, QYG, QMF, QKK, QRL, QOQ, QMJ, RBL, RBN, RJZ and RWW. STOP if adjudicated DIFFERENT or NOT_ORG admitted mentions exceed 0.5% of admitted coded mentions corpus-wide, or if any one code admits 3 or more of them. Sample baseline: 0 of 7,409.
- C3, refusal recall. Adjudicate every refused name with 2 or more mentions. If SAME refusals exceed 5% of letter- and zero-code mentions, add evidenced former-names entries and bump the version before U3. This is efficiency, not safety. Sample baseline: 2 of 7,402.
- C4. The census must show the plan untouched (pinned by a test).

**Repair (U3):**
- R1. The wet run holds against the dry plan's stored keys (notice, section, from_org, code, table version), per the 453 pattern. Any drift → stop.
- R2. Retire with a redirect only when a cluster empties into one identity org and no review table names it. Any other emptied cluster is listed and left. The dry plan must show 0 non-SAME clusters retired that the census did not see; the sample retires 34 SAME and 2 HOSTED clusters.
- R3. The first fold after arming must show 0 refusals of (value, name) pairs the census admitted, and 0 admissions it refused. That is the determinism check.
- R4. A sample re-resolve of repaired notices through a fresh armed resolver must agree 100% with the repaired bindings.
- R5. Wet only in a queue gap, with the arm disarmed until R1 passes.

**U7.** A pair whose witnesses are all refused by the check is hard-denied, as are pairs from codes the census showed admitting names of two adjudicated bodies.
designs.dependencies_and_order:
**Order:**
1. U0, the decision.
2. U1: table, function and census. Gate, deploy, dry altid run, then read C1-C4. No prevention ships here.
3. U2: arm plus repair, as one deploy with the arm disarmed.
4. U3: dry → read → wet, which arms the fold → project → verify.
5. 469 U7 (U4 here).

**469.** U7 needs U3's identity orgs and should also follow 469's own S5 read: no regrowth after the U5/U6 merges. U5's register alias is a prerequisite and is already deployed. It binds through the exact triple only, so it needs no change for NHS beyond the family entry. U4 of 469 (the planner) needs the witness-name check added to its NHS register keys. The planner's existing gates (single owner, cross-register, multi-PPON) stay. The check adds a structural deny for the review's hazards.

**518.** U7's alias bar for NHS targets inherits 518a's corroboration, which already ships with U5. Read 518's unit-1 refusal classes for the NHS family separately after U3. Optionally, let a GB-NHS alias bind be corroborated by the ODS check, which admitted 116 of 116 SAME PPON-holder names, to cut issue-518 regrowth there.

**519.** Independent of B's arm: digit-bearing codes are untouched, and RO98 is never allowlisted. 519 should land before or with U7, as its own text says, so U7 pairs one org per body. B's frozen table (RO98 sub-ICB records, inactive and five-character codes) is 519's natural classification input. Typo codes like RF1 could later be routed through the same check, by verdict rather than shape.

**Deferred.** The twin consolidation (U5, design C territory) can follow without touching B.

1. **Net effect stays weak.** B fixes the mint and the bind, not consolidation. About 90% of each body's mentions (median coded share 9.7%) stay on uncoded name clusters. Org counts go 355 → 449 → 334, and 12 codes end worse after U7.
2. **Overfitting.** The gate's rules were refined on this same sample: the role and descriptor levels, prefix-6 matching, the coverage ½ floor and the agent markers. The synthetic test reuses the sample's names. The only truly blind evidence will be C2: the 35 unlisted holders and the corpus.
3. **Simulation approximation.** Each holder's head name stood in for its coded mentions' names. That is valid under issue 234's exact name_norm binding, but not for clusters that merges have fed.
4. **Renames without a predecessor link.** RWW passes only because its old name's words live on in Inactive predecessors RKC and RJS. A pure self-rename is refused (status quo), and the remedy is a curated former-names column: a small second register, with evidence per entry.
5. **Predecessor policy.** Only Inactive predecessors count. 8 records with Active status are legally ended 2026-03-31 (QJG, QMJ, QMM, QNQ, QXU, RNK, RY2, RYV). These codes still mint for their era's notices, and post-merger successor names under them are refused — missed merges.

8. **Head names.** A mint takes the earliest admitted name. A HOSTED trading name could become the head if it is earliest, and no code re-elects head names.
9. **Bare codes.** 75 bare three-character raws (non-FTS) stay name-bound.

designs.name: Design C: reviewed NHS body consolidation (no mint). Members-exact verdicts merge a body's SAME clusters into its PPON org, and an alias armed from the merge ledger replays the merge in every fold and in a rebuild.
designs.summary:
This design mints no identity. For each ODS-confirmed three-character code, a reviewer and a challenger read every holder org. A HIGH merge verdict that is members-exact over the full holder set then folds the body's SAME provisional spelling clusters, plus its SAME PPON org or orgs, into one survivor:
- the PPON org where the body has an adjudicated SAME PPON (116 bodies);
- otherwise the body's largest spelling cluster, kept as a provisional anchor (13 bodies).

Each loser gets an `org_merge_log` row (rule `nhs-body`), so its id redirects 308 through `read::resolve_org`. The ODS code is written onto the survivor as a lookup-only merged identifier, `GBNHS<code>`.

**What I found in the code.** No existing path can do this, and nothing replays it:
- R2, E0 and R3 group by identifier keys, so a provisional row is never a member. 362's verdicts only admit groups those planners name.
- The 469 register planner refuses GB-NHS at `registry-shape` (crosswalk.rs:1208 `REGISTRIES` has no NHS; test at crosswalk.rs:1585). Its D3 gate also requires the register org to carry the identity as its own identifier (canonical.rs:23960-23978).
- The 234 reuse probe only finds `identifier IS NULL` rows (canonical.rs:17355-17360). So once a cluster is merged into a canonical row, the very next uncoded mention of that spelling mints a new provisional.
- A rebuild "re-mints every org from its mentions, so the merges … are undone" (canonical.rs:12054-12059).

The design therefore ships the wet merge together with a resolver alias, the same pattern as 448's and 469's PPON aliases.

**How the alias works.**
- It is armed at every fold from the `nhs-body` ledger rows. It reads only identity-keyed evidence and never org ids: (name_norm, country) → target, and a loser PPON → target.
- It runs in the identifier-less branch, before the 234 probe.
- It binds a reviewed spelling to the org that carries the target PPON triple (exact `org_of` probe), or for an anchor body to the anchor's 234 key.
- When the target is absent (a rebuild in notice-id order), it mints it deterministically from the ledger, so a rebuild reproduces the consolidated state without any job re-run.
- New spellings and stray clusters behave exactly as today (234). They reach a body only through the next review. The alias never binds by code.

**What it achieves, measured on the 129 listed bodies.**
- Orgs go from 352 to 129, or to 173 now: 11 capped bodies wait for their 35 unlisted holders to be adjudicated.
- Each survivor holds 100% of its body's listed mentions (60,399 in total). Today the canonical PPON org holds a median 13.9%; a mint's identity org would hold the coded share, a median 8.2%.
- Strays moved: 0. Junk identities minted: 0.

**What it needs.** An explicit owner decision recorded against 300 §10 ("No provisional↔canonical capture on name equality"), scoped to reviewed keys only. The alias does nothing until a reviewed wet run writes ledger rows, so prevention cannot act before the census.

designs.refold_invariance:
**How each merge class persists today**
- **Refolding a standing notice keeps its recorded binding.** `publishes()` compares only name, country, raw_identifier and scheme. Its doc says "Merges, rehomings, dissolves and case verdicts move recorded mentions … re-deciding every unchanged mention would undo them all" (canonical.rs:10255-10269). So C's repointed mentions stay put through incremental refolds.
- **New, stale (434) and rebuilt mentions are re-resolved**, so every merge class needs a resolver-side replay keyed by identity:
  - r2/e0, including 362's verdict-admitted groups: the canonical-key prevention, `canon_hit` at canonical.rs:16790-16822;
  - r3: anchors;
  - e2-altid (448 and 469 U5): the ledger alias, "identity to identity, never org ids, so it survives a rebuild's renumbering" (`ALTID_ALIAS_LEDGER_SQL` canonical.rs:6257, `arm_altid_alias` 15900ff, registry exact-triple bind 16137-16145);
  - rekey: identifier verdicts' `applied_literal` (15713-15760);
  - p0/p1: identical name_norm, which is the 234 key itself (ledger 29272-29290).
- **merged_hit (canonical.rs:16856-16872, cached at 17225-17230)** replays only issue 470's folded literals. GBNHS values have no canonical key (crosswalk.rs:425-430, `_ => None`), so they never reach it.
- **The orphan sweep** writes `org_sweep_log`, not `org_merge_log` (32759-32790), so it leaves no redirect.

**Why no existing path survives**
- `org_merge_verdicts.members` are org ids (DDL 610-633), consulted only at plan time (`merge_verdict_for` 25567-25600; admission `v.members == live` at 19260 and 24062). They go stale when a rebuild renumbers ids, unlike the triple-keyed identifier verdicts (645-652).
- A rebuild (`clear_canonical` 10707-10760; strip at 12030-12062) keeps `org_merge_log` and every verdict table. It drops the orgs, mentions, names and `organization_merged_identifiers`: "the merges these rows describe are undone" (12054-12059).
- The rebuild resolves in notice-id order (canonical.rs:10790; project.rs:2041-2045), so a body's uncoded TED and text-era history resolves years before its first PPON mention.
- Without U4, a merged spelling regrows on the very next fold, not just in a rebuild. The 234 probe needs `identifier IS NULL` (17355-17360), the loser row is deleted, and the branch mints (17366-17385).

**What C produces**
- **Incremental fold:** standing mentions stay on the survivor. Reviewed spellings, whether coded or uncoded, bind the survivor through the alias. Loser PPONs bind it at 448's bar. Unreviewed spellings and stray clusters bind exactly as before, because C never moved them. Steady state equals the merged state.
- **Full rebuild from archives:**
  - the first mention of a body, in any form, creates its single org deterministically. A PPON-coded mention takes the E0 mint (the PPON triple). A reviewed-spelling mention makes the alias mint the same triple, named by the ledger's `keep_name`. An anchor body is minted under its anchor 234 key.
  - every later mention of the body binds that org through `org_of` or the alias.
  - non-member clusters are re-minted by 234 exactly as they stand today.
  - the merged identifiers (GBNHS<code>, loser PPONs) are re-recorded on bind (the 460 D5 pattern, `record_alias_identifier` 4908-4931).
  - the result is the consolidated state, with no job re-run and no verdict re-admission.
- **Differences from steady state:** org ids renumber, so pre-rebuild ids are void by design (`feed_generation` bump at 10743). Head names come from the ledger's `keep_name` rather than a first-seen mention.

**Persistence of merges, verdicts and aliases**
- The merge persists through the repointed rows plus `org_merge_log` rule `nhs-body`. The ledger's identity evidence (name_norms with raw names, the PPON or anchor target, the code) is the replay record. Verdicts are only the admission record.
- Chains are resolved at arm time: an anchor later folded into a PPON survivor follows on, a PPON later folded by 469 follows its e2-altid target, and a cycle poisons the key.
- A future change to `org_name_norm` requires re-keying the ledger from the raw names stored in the evidence (the p1 precedent at 29690-29700).
- The alias is inert with zero ledger rows, so the deploy alone changes nothing.
designs.false_merge_risk:
**Merge set.** 352 listed SAME orgs fold into 129 survivors. Unit 1's adjudication agreed on 392 of 393 claims, with 0 disputed. The one unverified row (TAJ's PPON) carries a wrong org id in adjudication-rows.json. Members-exact admission over the live holder set refuses such a verdict, and verdicts must be built from the planner's listing.

**Residual risks and their guards**
1. **A wrong SAME verdict fuses two bodies.** Guards:
   - reviewer plus challenger, HIGH only on agreement;
   - ODS name, predecessor and successor read;
   - the best-match ODS score shown to the reviewer. It flags 6 of 235 SAME holders, 106 of whose 109 coded mentions are RWW's rename. A HIGH SAME on a flagged holder needs cited ODS rename evidence;
   - 362's KIO bar: distinct institutions or sibling units with 20 or more mentions on the smaller side are parked at medium;
   - HOSTED_OR_SITE holders (9 registry, 1 PPON) are never members.
2. **A newcomer cluster is fused unread.** Blocked by `reviewed_holders` exact equality, so a new holder makes the verdict stale. The 35 unlisted holders hold 11 bodies until they are adjudicated.
3. **Cross-body orgs.** 8 orgs are SAME for one code and DIFFERENT for another (Walton Centre: RET/REN; UHB: RRK/RJE; and others). Each is a member of its SAME body only. An org proposed as SAME for two codes is contested and held. There are 0 in the corrected data.
4. **Legal-end codes (7).** A successor publishing under a predecessor's name could be captured by the predecessor body. Guards: the planner denies members whose name matches a successor's ODS name, and the reviewer reads post-legal-end mentions. A resolver date fence would need the notice date on `Mention` (canonical.rs:4480-4495); that is an open risk.
5. **The alias captures a homonym in future.** A different body publishing an exact reviewed name binds to this canonical body. The same mention would already bind the provisional cluster today under 234, so the risk is no wider, but it is more visible. Guards: exact (name_norm, country) only, reviewed names only, a name claimed by two bodies is poisoned, the generic and consortium checks run at plan time, and S4 regrowth reads.

designs.stop_rules:
**S0, the census gate (before any wet run and before any verdict is POSTed).** The `nhs-body` dry plan lists every holder uncapped, and every holder of a body under verdict is adjudicated, with 0 unlisted. Until then a body is held, which is 11 bodies and 35 holders today. U4 cannot act before this: it arms only from ledger rows, which only an admitted wet run writes. That is how "prevention does not ship before its census gate" holds structurally.

**S1, verdict quality.** Stop the campaign if any of these holds:
- challenger agreement on SAME claims falls below 98% (unit 1: 392 of 393);
- more than 3% of the HIGH SAME holders are best-match-flagged without cited ODS rename or predecessor evidence (measured 6 of 235, 2.6%, including the RWW rename);
- any HIGH SAME member's name matches a successor ODS name.

**S2, wet parity.** Abort before any write if the live plan and the stored plan differ by more than max(2%, 5) bodies.

**S3, capped first wet run.** `max_groups` 20. Read every `nhs_body_merged` entry:
- the survivor is the reviewed one;
- no non-member org is touched;
- the survivor's mentions equal the sum of its members' (plus mentions arriving since);
- each loser answers 308, and `?identifier=GBNHS<code>` answers the survivor.

Any defect stops the run. The fix is a keep verdict plus a scoped unwind.

**S4, regrowth on every fold and dry run.** Alias counters (asked, bound, minted, refused by cause) on each fold. Halt if refusals exceed binds. Halt if the next dry plan's `nhs_body_regrown` is non-zero, meaning a ledger key or loser PPON stands on a live row other than its target. Newcomer holders with unreviewed names are expected and go to the next cohort, not into S4.

**S5, refold and rebuild proof.**
- The store test rebuilds in notice-id order and must give one org per body.
- On prod, a refold canary (the 300 tripwire-7 pattern): refold 3 notices for each of 3 consolidated bodies (an uncoded TED notice, a coded FTS notice, a PPON-first notice). Zero bindings may move.

**S6, rollback fence.** After the first wet run, no binary rollback to a build that predates U4 unless the merges are first unwound. Such a binary ignores `nhs-body` ledger rows, so every merged spelling would regrow. This goes in the deploy note.

designs.open_risks:
1. **Policy.** The standing alias is "provisional↔canonical capture on name equality", which 300 §10 names explicitly (line 1014). It needs the owner's recorded, scoped exception. ADR 0003's amendment covers Tender identity only (line 63).
2. **Coverage.** Spelling clusters that never carry the code cannot be reached by the code harvest, and their number is unknown. They stay split until a 300 Stage-4 E3 edge review proposes them. All figures cover listed holders only.
3. **Rebuild mint-if-absent.** In a rebuild, U4 writes a PPON triple onto a row that a name-bound mention created. The identity is reviewed and equals the steady-state survivor's, but this is new resolver behaviour. The head name comes from the ledger, not from a first-seen mention.
4. **Anchor bodies stay provisional.** 13 survivors keep `provisional:1` and a NULL identifier:
   - QJG, QWE, QYG and RJN have published PPONs that never minted an org;
   - QOX and RXM have no PPON org either.
   A later PPON org arrives as a newcomer holder that needs review. Until then, a PPON-first mention mints the PPON org beside the anchor.
5. **Legal-end date fence.** The 7 codes ended on 2026-03-31 cannot be fenced by date in the resolver without adding the notice date to `Mention` (canonical.rs:4480-4495). Review and the successor-name gate are the only guards.
6. **No automatic undo.** A bad merge needs a scoped dissolve job, and none exists for `nhs-body`. Mitigation is the capped wet run and the S3 read.
7. **Rehomed and case-moved mentions** on member clusters move with the merge. A rebuild re-resolves them by name, because `org_mention_rehoming` is not read by the resolver. That is a non-invariance of rehoming that predates C. The planner flags these members (review keep-set, 32543-32588).
8. **Chains.** A PPON survivor later folded by 448 or 469 must be followed, not re-minted. U4's chain rule handles it; 0 such NHS pairs exist today, but it needs its own test.
9. **Review cost.** 223 merges plus 35 unadjudicated holders, roughly twice 469 U6's campaign.
10. **Stack and performance.** Boxing is required (run_project budget 9,000 B). The arm reads a few hundred ledger rows through a partial index, and a bind is a HashMap probe. A mint-if-absent adds at most one INSERT per body per rebuild.
11. **Adjudication input defect.** The TAJ PPON org id is wrong in adjudication-rows.json. Any tooling that builds verdicts from that file would post a verdict that members-exact admission rejects.

On the correctness lens the ranking is C (7), then B (6), then A (5). I recommend C, on two conditions:
- alias keys are limited to the member rows' own 234 keys (member name_norm, GB), and the planner denies any key that is the 234 key of a standing identifier-NULL row outside the body;
- a scoped unwind (retire the nhs-body ledger rows, then a dissolve that re-resolves the survivor's former members) is built and tested before the full wet run.

Why C:
- It is the only design where an unreviewed stray, or one the sample never contained, cannot bind to the wrong body. The code is never a binding key, and it mints no identity.
- Its merges are reviewed, members-exact and replayable from the ledger.
- It leaves Tender planning alone.

A is the weakest on correctness:
- It moves Tender planning without saying so. buyer_key becomes identifier-keyed, and the FTS ocid refusal at two or more distinct buyer keys (canonical.rs:14088) then splits some procedures and welds others. Its resolver-only pins cannot reach the projection.

result.decision:
## Decision (unit 2, second) — 2026-10-11

This replaces the withdrawn D1–D4. All three judges ranked design C first. Counts are over distinct orgs: 352 SAME orgs across 129 bodies.

**D1. No mint. Consolidate each body by review (design C).**
- One verdict per allowlisted code, HIGH and members-exact, folds the body's SAME clusters and its SAME PPON org into one survivor.
- The survivor is the PPON org. For RYA it is the PPON of the real code. A body with no PPON org keeps its largest SAME cluster as a provisional anchor.
- Each loser gets an `org_merge_log` row with rule `nhs-body`, so its id answers 308.
- The survivor records `GBNHS<code>` as a merged identifier.
- `normalise_identifier` does not change.

*Why:*
- Orgs go from 352 to 173 now, and to 129 once the remaining holders are read. No body ends worse, no stray moves, and no identity is minted.
- A mint would hold only about 9.5% of a body's mentions.
- The code never binds a mention, so strays nobody has reviewed cannot bind to the wrong body. B4's name check, by contrast, admits 'University of Oxford' under RTH.

**D2. Amend 300 §10 in writing.** A body verdict that is reviewed, ODS-confirmed and members-exact may fold provisional clusters into a canonical row and arm an alias for its reviewed keys. Nothing else may capture by name.

**D3. A frozen ODS table and check, pure, in ingest.**
- The table is B's: 1,053 codes, with RO98, Inactive and five-character codes kept as rivals. It also holds predecessor names, the RO107 and RO172 lists, and a version string.
- A's 213-code allowlist decides which codes may have a survivor.
- The B4 check gains two refusals:
  - non-NHS institutions (university, council or ltd with no NHS role token);
  - ties.
- A member the check refuses needs a HIGH verdict that cites ODS rename or predecessor evidence. RCX 'Queen Elizabeth Hospital FT' is held.

*Why:* the review is checked against ODS, and the check itself never binds anything.

**D4. Alias keys are the members' own 234 keys** (head `name_norm`, GB). If a standing identifier-NULL row outside the body already owns a key, that key is denied (`alias_key_owned_elsewhere`) and its member is held.
*Why:* the 234 path matches on head names (canonical.rs ~17357), so the alias can never bind more widely than 234 does today.

**D5. The alias reaches its target through `Some(identifier)`, on a synthesised PPON identifier** (org_of → rekey → canon_of → altid alias → mint). Any mint of a ledger target takes the ledger's `keep_name`.
*Why:* if a later fold absorbs a survivor, the alias follows it instead of minting a new row, and the head name no longer depends on which mention came first.

**D6. These are never members:**
- HOSTED_OR_SITE, NOT_ORG and DIFFERENT holders;
- orgs that carry a minted identity (519's);
- successor names under the 7 legally-ended codes;
- generic or consortium names;
- members flagged as rehomed or case-moved.

The QKK/QMF cross-assignment is dropped because it fails members ⊆ live, so both bodies stay anchors.

Verdicts are built from the live listing only. adjudication-rows.json gives TAJ's PPON as 31542073, which is QMM's PPON org.

**D7. A scoped `nhs-body` unwind ships with the wet path and is tested before any wet run.** It retires a body's ledger rows, then dissolves the body back through 234/E0.
*Why:* nothing can undo these 223 merges today.

**D8. Any future forward arm goes in the resolver, never in `normalise_identifier`.** It binds to the survivor's merged identifier, never to a newly minted twin.
*Why:* the identifier feeds buyer_key and the FTS ocid gate (canonical.rs:14088).

### Units
- **U0:** this record, the 300 amendment, and the u1 corrections: NHS TRUST is 99, uncoded is 47,467, and the TAJ id.
- **U1:** D3's table and check. No behaviour change.
- **U2:** the census, a dry `nhs-body` run. It reports:
  - every holder, uncapped;
  - who owns each key, the check's verdicts and the D6 flags;
  - country-less and bare GB-NHS values;
  - tails not on the allowlist;
  - the coded share by notice year.

  It also adds `reviewed_holders` and 1-member verdicts. Deploy it dry.
- **U3:** adjudicate the 35 unread holders (reviewer plus challenger) and POST the verdicts. Post 469 keep verdicts for the QKK, QMF, RXX, RTF, RGT, 0CX and RAL PPON pairs.
- **U4:** one deploy, after 491 3(b) leaves canonical.rs and supervisor.rs. It carries:
  - the wet path;
  - the alias armed from the ledger (boxed);
  - the D7 unwind;
  - the `nhs_body_merged` and `nhs_body_regrown` reports;
  - the re-resolve read.
- **U5:** dry run, then a capped wet run (20 bodies), then the read, then the full wet run.
- **U6 (conditional):** D8's arm.
  - It opens only if the coded share over the last 12 months is above 9.5% and S4 shows new coded spellings regrowing.
  - It ships only if its own dry census admits at most 0.5% non-SAME names.

### Stop rules
- **S0:**
  - No verdict for a body that has an unread holder (11 such bodies today).
  - No key owned elsewhere is admitted.
- **S1:**
  - Agreement on SAME is at least 98%.
  - No flagged member is admitted without cited evidence.
  - No successor-name member is admitted.
- **S2:** the live plan matches the stored plan within max(2%, 5) bodies, or the run aborts before writing.
- **S3:** the capped read shows:
  - every survivor is the reviewed one;
  - non-members are untouched;
  - each survivor's mentions equal the sum of its members';
  - every loser answers 308;
  - `?identifier=GBNHS<code>` answers the survivor for 20 codes.
- **S4:**
  - On every fold, alias refusals are no more than binds.
  - On every dry run, `nhs_body_regrown` is 0.
- **S5:**
  - A store test that rebuilds in notice order gives one org per body.
  - On prod, 3 notices for each of 3 bodies (TED uncoded, FTS coded, PPON-first), re-resolved through a fresh resolver, agree 100%.
- **S6:** no rollback to a binary older than U4 unless the unwind runs first.

### Handoffs
- **469 U7:**
  - covers digit-bearing NHS codes only;
  - its ODS confirmation and witness check use D3's table;
  - REGISTRIES gets no letter-only shape;
  - survivors count as holders through their merged identifiers;
  - the keep verdicts deny the cross-body pairs.
- **519:**
  - takes the RO98 sub-ICB codes (including the 10 Active `00[A-Z]`) and the typo codes;
  - their orgs never join a body;
  - D3's table classifies them, and A's (triple, name_norm) pin is a candidate fix;
  - it lands before U7 or with it.

### Trade-offs accepted
- No `GBNHS` identity is minted; lookups go through merged identifiers.
- Spelling clusters that never carry the code stay split (E3).
- New coded spellings regrow until the next review cohort, and a newcomer holder makes the verdicts stale.
- 13 anchor bodies stay provisional.
- The review costs about twice 469 U6.
- Hosted sites stay separate orgs.
- The legally-ended codes have no date fence.

---

**Points the judges did not settle**
1. **Head name of a survivor minted in a rebuild.** Correctness wants the ODS name, through A's naming hook. C uses the ledger's `keep_name`, and B uses the earliest admitted name. D5 takes `keep_name`, which follows how publishers write the name rather than ODS's uppercase.
2. **How strong the D3 check is in the planner.** Correctness and engineering want a structural denial or flag that needs cited evidence to override. Product and C's original design treat it as an aid for reviewers only. D3 takes the flag with cited evidence.
3. **How wide the alias keys are.** Correctness allows only the members' head 234 keys. Product would also arm mention-name norms that no standing 234 row owns. D4 takes the stricter rule.
4. **When the unwind must exist.** Product says before the first wet run, correctness before the full wet run. Engineering does not require it, since 469 shipped without one. D7 takes "before any wet run".
5. **QKK/QMF.** The options were to drop the cross-assignment, or to build an explicit cross-code membership path that reads both codes' holder sets (correctness's alternative). D6 drops it.
6. **Whether a `GBNHS` identity is ever minted.** Correctness would allow a later mint built from B's gate plus A's pins and A's two-way re-bind. Product and engineering want only a resolver arm that binds to C's merged-identifier holder, and only if the census shows recent notices are mostly coded. D8 and U6 encode the second view.
7. **Whether 469 keep verdicts are needed under C at all.** Only engineering asked for them; the registry-shape gate already denies these pairs. U3 includes them as cheap insurance.
8. **Numbers not reconciled.** Mentions on PPON rows: 5,073 (product) against 5,086 (C). A's org count: 447 against 448. The 26,074 repointed mentions were not checked by any judge.

I re-ran the correctness judge's probe of B4 myself to confirm the 'University of Oxford' under RTH admit cited in D1. A scratch copy of the decision is at /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-tender-db/3050fd14-5ca6-5dd7-8b63-f827e13fd8ce/scratchpad/panel/synth/decision.md.
